services.h1: Pest Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Living in Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Orlando, and Winter Park means dealing with pests in every season. With warm weather and afternoon rains through much of the year, ants, roaches, spiders, and rodents never really go away, they just shift where they hide.

Orlando Pest Pros provides steady, year-round protection built for Central Florida homes. We focus on keeping pests out in the first place, explaining what we find in plain language, and treating your home with care and respect.

pests.name: Palmetto Bugs
pests.blurb: These large American cockroaches thrive in mulch beds, sewers, and palm trees, then slip inside during summer rains when they take flight. We seal common entry points and treat harborage areas around the exterior so fewer make it indoors.

pests.name: Ghost Ants
pests.blurb: Tiny ghost ants love Florida kitchens and bathrooms, trailing to moisture and sweets from wall voids and mulch. We track trails to the colony and use targeted baits that workers carry back, rather than just spraying what you see.

pests.name: Fire Ants
pests.blurb: After summer storms, fire ant mounds pop up fast in Kissimmee and St. Cloud lawns, making yards painful for kids and pets. We treat mounds directly and manage foraging colonies around the property to keep activity down between visits.

pests.name: Roof Rats
pests.blurb: Roof rats are at home in Central Florida attics and citrus trees, traveling along fences and rooflines at night. We inspect for droppings, rub marks, and entry gaps, then combine trapping, exclusion guidance, and exterior reduction to discourage them.

pests.name: Spiders
pests.blurb: Wolf spiders, house spiders, and widow spiders find plenty of insects to hunt around porches, garages, and lanais. We remove webs, reduce harborage, and treat eaves and entry points so spiders move elsewhere.

pests.name: Millipedes and Earwigs
pests.blurb: Heavy rain drives millipedes and earwigs out of mulch and into garages and doorways across Orlando neighborhoods. We focus on the landscape edge, door thresholds, and moisture areas to break that indoor push.

pests.name: Silverfish
pests.blurb: Silverfish favor humid bathrooms, closets, and boxes stored in Florida garages, feeding on paper and fabrics. We address moisture and hiding spots indoors while protecting the exterior to cut off new arrivals.

sections.heading: Why Central Florida homes need year-round protection
body: Central Florida never gets a true winter kill-off, so pest colonies keep feeding and breeding straight through the cooler months. What looks quiet in winter is often just pests moving deeper into walls, attics, and mulch until warmth and rain bring them back out.

Add in stucco homes, tile roofs, dense landscaping, and nearby ponds or conservation areas, and you have ideal shelter for palmetto bugs, ants, and roof rats. Regular exterior care through the year matters far more here than a single spray, because pressure builds again after every storm.

sections.heading: What's included in every visit
body: Every visit starts with a careful walk around your home, looking at door sweeps, weep holes, hose bibs, lanai screens, and the mulch line where pests travel. Inside, we listen to your concerns, check kitchens, baths, and the garage, and explain what we are seeing without jargon.

Treatment focuses on the outside first, creating a protective zone around the foundation, entry points, and harborage spots, with careful interior spot care only where needed. We sweep webs, note conditions that invite pests like standing water or dense ground cover, and leave you with simple next steps.

sections.heading: Safe for kids, pets, and Florida wildlife
body: We know Orlando-area families share yards with pets, pollinators, lizards, and birds, and we treat with that in mind. Our technicians apply products in a targeted way around cracks, crevices, and entry points, avoiding broad coverage where kids and pets play.

You will always know what was done and how to get the most from it, like when to let treatments settle before watering or letting pets back into a treated area. If you have a vegetable garden, pond, butterfly planting, or bromeliads, just point it out and we will work around it thoughtfully.

process.detail: We walk your home inside and out, from the attic to the mulch line, and listen to what you have been seeing. You get a clear picture of current activity and the conditions inviting pests in.
We explain what we found, what we will treat, and what you can do to help keep pests out. There is no pressure, just honest guidance built for your home and yard.
We protect the exterior perimeter and entry points first, with focused interior care in kitchens, baths, and other hot spots. Webs are swept and gaps are noted for sealing.

Because Florida pressure never stops, we return on a regular schedule to renew protection and adjust for rains and swarms. If activity flares between visits, just call Orlando Pest Pros and we will make it right.

faqs.q: Why do I need pest control all year in Central Florida?
faqs.a: Our warm, humid climate lets ants, roaches, spiders, and rodents stay active through every season. Without steady exterior protection, new pests move in after each rain, swarm, or landscaping change.

faqs.q: Is your treatment safe around kids and pets?
faqs.a: Yes, when applied as directed and allowed to settle. We use targeted applications in cracks, crevices, and exterior entry points, and we will give you simple guidance on watering, play areas, and pet access after each visit.

faqs.q: Why do palmetto bugs fly inside during summer?
faqs.a: Palmetto bugs live outdoors in mulch, palms, and sewers and take flight during warm, rainy evenings. They slip through open garage doors, gaps under doors, and torn screens, which is why we focus so much on the exterior and entry points.

faqs.q: Do I need to leave my home during service?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Interior care is focused and low-disruption, and exterior care is done around the perimeter and yard. We will let you know if a particular area should be avoided briefly while it settles.

faqs.q: What if pests come back between visits?
faqs.a: That can happen after heavy storms or when mulch and moisture shift. Just call Orlando Pest Pros and describe what you are seeing, and we will return to re-check and touch up as covered under your plan.

services.metaDescription: Protect your Central Florida home from subterranean & Formosan termites with expert inspections, bait systems & barriers by Orlando Pest Pros near Orlando.
services.h1: Termite Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Termites are the quiet threat behind many Central Florida walls, working unseen in soil, mulch, and damp wood while homes look fine from the street. In our area, both native subterranean termites and aggressive Formosan termites swarm in spring after rain and can find even small gaps near the foundation.

Orlando Pest Pros helps Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Orlando, and Winter Park homeowners catch activity early and choose protection that fits Florida soil and weather. We explain what we find in clear terms and recommend lasting solutions, not scare tactics.

pests.name: Subterranean Termites
pests.blurb: Native subterranean colonies live in the soil and build mud tubes up foundations to reach framing and siding. We look for tubes, swarm wings, and moisture damage, then protect the soil line and structure with proven methods.

pests.name: Formosan Termites
pests.blurb: Formosan termites form very large colonies and forage aggressively, sometimes nesting above ground where moisture collects. We pay close attention to rooflines, wall voids, and AC moisture areas where they can gain a foothold.

pests.name: Drywood Termites
pests.blurb: Drywood termites live entirely inside dry wood like fascia, cabinets, and furniture, leaving tiny pellets behind. We inspect attics and trim closely and recommend focused wood treatments where activity is found.

pests.name: Dampwood Termites
pests.blurb: Dampwood termites favor very moist or decaying wood around leaks, rotting eaves, and wood-to-soil contact. We help identify moisture sources and damaged wood that should be repaired along with treatment.

pests.name: Carpenter Ants (Often Confused With Termites)
pests.blurb: Winged carpenter ants are often mistaken for termite swarmers by Orlando homeowners in spring. Unlike termites, they carve galleries in moist wood to nest, and we can sort out which pest you have and treat it correctly.

sections.heading: Termite swarm season in Central Florida
body: After warm spring rains, termite swarmers take flight in the evening to start new colonies, often gathering around porch lights and windows. Finding discarded wings on sills or in cobwebs in Kissimmee and Orlando homes is a classic sign that a mature colony is nearby.

Formosan swarmers tend to appear as days stay warm and humid, while native subterranean swarmers often show in spring daylight after rain. Any swarm indoors, or mud tubes along the foundation and garage, deserves a prompt professional look before damage spreads.

sections.heading: Bait systems vs. liquid barriers: what actually works here
body: Both modern bait systems and liquid soil barriers can protect Central Florida homes when they are installed carefully and monitored over time. Baits use stations around the home that foraging termites share with the colony, which suits our sandy soils and high water tables in many neighborhoods.

Liquid barriers create a treated zone in the soil that termites must pass through to reach the structure, which suits homes with clear soil access and stable grading. We will walk your lot, irrigation, ponds, and construction type with you and recommend the approach that will hold up best there.

sections.heading: WDO inspections for home buyers and sellers
body: In Osceola and Orange Counties, wood-destroying organism inspections are a common part of buying or selling, especially around older block homes with wood framing and additions. We provide thorough, documented inspections of accessible areas, noting live activity, past damage, and conditions like wood-to-soil contact or excess moisture.

Our reports use plain language and photos so buyers, sellers, and agents all understand what was seen. If treatment or repairs are needed, we explain options clearly so your closing can move forward with confidence.

process.detail: We check the foundation, crawl areas, garage, attic, and exterior soil line for tubes, wings, pellets, and moisture. You get an honest explanation of what we found and where.
We show you photos and signs in plain language and outline bait, barrier, or wood treatment choices for your home. We tailor the plan to your construction, yard, and moisture conditions.
Our team installs stations or treats the soil line with care around irrigation, plantings, and drainage. Inside, we treat affected wood areas tidily and with respect for your home.
Termite protection works best with regular checks through Florida seasons. We return to inspect stations and barriers, watch for new swarm signs, and adjust for landscaping or moisture changes.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have termites or flying ants?
faqs.a: Termite swarmers have straight antennae, broad waists, and wings of equal length that shed easily, while flying ants have elbowed antennae and narrow waists. If you find piles of wings on windowsills after a rainy evening, save a few in a bag and call Orlando Pest Pros for identification.

faqs.q: What are mud tubes on my block wall or foundation?
faqs.a: Mud tubes are sheltered highways subterranean termites build from soil to wood. Finding them along the foundation, garage wall, or lanai means foragers are active and your home should be inspected promptly.

faqs.q: Are Formosan termites worse than regular subterranean termites?
faqs.a: Formosan colonies can grow much larger and forage over wider areas, so they can damage wood faster once established. The good news is that careful inspection, moisture control, and steady bait or barrier protection are effective against both types.

faqs.q: Will mulch and irrigation around my home attract termites?
faqs.a: Heavy mulch piled against stucco and frequent watering that keeps soil moist can make conditions more inviting. We will show you how to keep mulch pulled back from the foundation and irrigation directed away from the wall while still keeping plants healthy.

faqs.q: Do I need a WDO inspection when buying in Kissimmee or Orlando?
faqs.a: Many buyers request one for peace of mind, and some lenders expect it, given our heavy termite pressure. Our inspection documents visible activity and damage in accessible areas and gives you clear next steps before closing.

services.h1: Mosquito Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: In the Orlando metro, mosquitoes are part of life from spring through fall and often all year near lakes, ponds, and ditches. Retention ponds, roadside ditches, bromeliads, clogged gutters, and lake edges give them endless places to breed within flight range of your patio.

Orlando Pest Pros helps you take your yard back with barrier treatments and breeding-site reduction, while being honest about results. No company can eliminate every mosquito in Central Florida, but steady control can make evenings outside far more comfortable.

pests.name: Mosquitoes
pests.blurb: Our local mosquitoes breed in still water as small as a saucer and rest in shady shrubs and tall grass by day. We treat resting areas and help you find hidden water sources so fewer adults reach your family.

pests.name: Biting Midges
pests.blurb: Biting midges thrive around damp soil, lake edges, and retention areas and slip through ordinary screens. Yard treatments that calm mosquitoes also help reduce these tiny biters around lanais and docks.

pests.name: No-See-Ums
pests.blurb: No-see-ums are most active around dawn and dusk and leave itchy welts that feel out of proportion to their size. We focus on shaded resting spots and breezy patio edges where they gather.

pests.name: Stable Flies and Other Yard Biters
pests.blurb: Stable flies and similar biters breed in moist organic matter and annoy pets and people near kennels, compost, and grass clippings. We point out sanitation and moisture fixes while treating harborage to ease pressure.

pests.name: Ticks in Shady Yards
pests.blurb: Ticks wait in tall grass, leaf litter, and along fence lines where pets and wildlife pass in our warm climate. During mosquito visits we can review those edge areas and treat harborage to support broader yard comfort.

sections.heading: Where mosquitoes breed in Central Florida yards
body: Most backyard mosquitoes come from very close by, not miles away. In Kissimmee, St. Cloud, and Orlando we routinely find larvae in bromeliads, saucers under pots, toys, tarps, clogged gutters, and low spots along ditches and retention ponds.

Lake edges, conservation swales, and neighbor yards can also send adults drifting over on calm evenings. That is why we walk the whole property with you, tip and drain what we can, and note what needs trimming, cleaning, or better drainage.

sections.heading: What barrier treatments can (and can't) do
body: Barrier treatments coat the undersides of leaves, shrubs, fences, and shaded structures where mosquitoes rest during the heat of the day. When mosquitoes land there, they pick up the treatment, which brings down the number trying to bite around patios and play areas.

What treatment cannot do is put a dome over your yard or stop new mosquitoes from flying in after rain. Nearby ponds and ditches will keep producing, so honest control means fewer bites and more usable evenings, not zero mosquitoes forever.

sections.heading: Rainy-season treatment cadence
body: Summer storms wash and regrow mosquito habitat almost weekly, with fresh broods hatching after each downpour. Steady visits through the rainy season keep the barrier fresh and let us re-check bromeliads, gutters, and containers that refilled since last time.

In drier stretches we can stretch the rhythm and focus more on harborage and source reduction. We will set a schedule that matches your yard, your lake or pond exposure, and how much time your family spends outside.

process.detail: We tour shaded resting spots, play areas, and patios while checking for standing water in containers and landscape pockets. You learn exactly where your mosquitoes are likely coming from.
We empty and tip what we can, clear debris that holds water, and suggest trims or drainage tweaks. Small changes to bromeliads, saucers, and gutters make a big difference.

We treat shrubs, ground cover, fence lines, and patio perimeters where mosquitoes rest, with care around blooms, gardens, and water features. The goal is comfort where you gather, not blanket coverage of the whole lot.
We return through the mosquito season to renew the barrier and catch new breeding after storms. Between visits, simple habits like refreshing pet bowls and clearing toys help keep numbers low.

faqs.q: Can you get rid of all mosquitoes in my yard?
faqs.a: No honest company can promise that in Central Florida, with ponds, ditches, and humid air all around. Our service greatly reduces biting pressure so you can enjoy your patio, though some mosquitoes will always drift in, especially after rain.

faqs.q: How long does a barrier treatment last?
faqs.a: Effectiveness depends on rain, sun, irrigation, and plant growth, with heavy storms breaking it down faster. Regular visits through the rainy season keep protection renewed and breeding spots checked.

faqs.q: Is mosquito treatment safe for my garden and pond?
faqs.a: We take care around edible gardens, pollinator plantings, and water features by treating resting foliage rather than open water or blooms. Point out ponds, bromeliads, and butterfly areas during the walk so we can work around them.

faqs.q: Why are mosquitoes worse after summer storms?
faqs.a: Storms refill every container, gutter, and ditch while scattering adults to new shelter. Eggs hatch quickly in warm water, so a calm week after rain often brings a fresh wave of biters.

faqs.q: What can I do between visits to help?
faqs.a: Tip water from toys and tarps, refresh pet bowls and birdbaths, keep gutters clear, and trim dense shrubs where mosquitoes rest. If bites spike after a storm, call Orlando Pest Pros and we will advise on timing for your next visit.

services.metaDescription: Trusted rodent control in Osceola & Orange Counties, FL from Orlando Pest Pros. We remove roof rats and mice, seal entry points, and restore attics safely.
services.h1: Rodent Control in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Living in Osceola and Orange Counties means dealing with rodents all year. Warm weather, backyard citrus, and dense Orlando neighborhoods give roof rats and mice steady food and shelter.

Once they reach your attic or garage, they nest quietly and keep coming back. Orlando Pest Pros finds how they get in, removes them carefully, and seals your home so they stay out. Our local team knows Central Florida construction and the habits that invite rats back.

pests.name: Roof Rats
pests.blurb: Our most common attic invader. Roof rats climb citrus, palms, and fences to reach rooflines, then nest in insulation and wall voids. Listen for night scurrying and watch for droppings near fruit trees.

pests.name: Norway Rats
pests.blurb: Heavier ground dwellers that burrow under slabs, sheds, and garden beds. Common near canals, ponds, and homes with pet food or open trash outside. They slip through garage gaps and vents to reach stored food.

pests.name: House Mice
pests.blurb: Small nesters that slip through gaps around pipes and doors. Kitchens, pantries, and garages offer crumbs and nesting material year round. They chew packaging and leave tiny droppings in cabinets and drawers.

pests.name: Cotton Rats
pests.blurb: Field rodents from overgrown lots, pond banks, and rural edges of Osceola County. Heavy rain and mowing push them toward sheds, garages, and lanais. They prefer dense cover but will shelter indoors when disturbed.

sections.heading: How rats get into Central Florida homes
body: Central Florida homes offer rats many hidden paths inside. Tile roofs, soffit vents, and plumbing chases run from yard to attic. Roof rats travel along citrus limbs, palms, and lines, then slip through lifted flashing or chewed vents.

At ground level, loose garage seals, open pipe gaps, and torn lanai screens invite mice and Norway rats. Fallen citrus, bird seed, pet bowls, and open trash feed them nearby. Once one finds a safe route, scent trails guide others all year.

sections.heading: Exclusion first: why sealing beats trapping alone
body: Traps catch the rodents you hear but leave open the gaps that invite the next family. With no real off season here, an unsealed home is quickly revisited. Lasting control starts with a full inspection of roofline, attic, garage, and crawl areas.

Orlando Pest Pros focuses on exclusion with durable materials that resist gnawing and humidity. We seal pipes, vents, eaves, and doors, reinforce weak soffits and screens, and add sweeps where needed. To plan lasting protection, call Orlando Pest Pros for a home specific inspection.

sections.heading: Attic cleanup and sanitation after removal
body: Rats soil insulation, chew wiring, and leave droppings and odor behind. In damp attics that mess lingers and can draw new rats and other pests. Proper cleanup removes contaminated material and helps your attic feel like home again.

After removal we check insulation, nesting debris, and gnawed spots. We remove droppings safely, refresh affected areas, and advise on ventilation and storage. You get clear guidance on what was affected and how to keep the attic clean and dry.

process.detail: We walk your roofline, attic, garage, and yard to find droppings, rub marks, and entries. You learn where rodents travel and what draws them near.
We place targeted traps in safe, strategic spots away from family and pets. We monitor activity and adjust until indoor pressure is gone and the attic is quiet.
We seal entries around eaves, vents, pipes, and doors with rodent resistant materials. We advise on branches, vines, and stored items that give rats cover and roof access.
We clear droppings and nesting debris and refresh soiled areas. You receive simple tips for food storage, yard care, and seasonal checks that help keep rodents out.

faqs.q: Why do I hear scratching in my attic at night?
faqs.a: Roof rats are night active and often nest in attics and wall voids. Warmth, shelter, and nearby citrus keep them active year round in Central Florida.

faqs.q: Are rodents a year round problem near Orlando?
faqs.a: Yes. Mild winters mean breeding and foraging never fully stop. Fallen fruit, irrigation, and open trash support them in every season.

faqs.q: Will traps alone solve a rat problem?
faqs.a: Traps reduce numbers but do not close entries. Without exclusion and sanitation, new rodents follow scent trails back inside.

faqs.q: Is attic cleanup really needed after rats leave?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Droppings, urine, and nesting material hold odor and can attract pests. Cleaning and refreshing affected areas helps prevent return visits.

faqs.q: How can I keep mice out of my kitchen?
faqs.a: Store dry goods in sealed containers and clear crumbs quickly. Seal gaps under sinks and around pipes, and keep garage and pantry clutter low.

services.h1: Bed Bug Treatment in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Waking up with itchy welts after travel or a rental stay is stressful, and bed bugs are a real possibility around Kissimmee, St. Cloud, and greater Orlando. These hitchhiking pests do not care how tidy your home is, and they settle in quickly once they arrive in luggage or furniture. As your local neighbor, Orlando Pest Pros helps you get clear answers without judgment or panic.

We serve homes, apartments, and short-term rentals across Osceola and Orange Counties with discreet, thorough service built for Florida living. From the first inspection to follow-up guidance, we explain what wefind in plain language and what to do next. If you suspect bed bugs, call Orlando Pest Pros and we will help you take the next calm step.

pests.name: Bed Bugs
pests.blurb: Bed bugs are small, flat, reddish-brown insects that hide by day and feed at night, often around mattresses, box springs, headboards, and nearby furniture. In Central Florida they stay active through every season, moving easily between bedrooms, living areas, and rental turnovers. Because they are excellent hiders, a small group tucked in a seam can grow into a widespread problem before you ever see activity in the open.

pests.name: Signs of Infestation
pests.blurb: Most people first notice itchy bites, tiny rust-colored spots on sheets, shed skins, or a faint musty odor near the bed. You may also spot live bugs along mattress seams, behind headboards, inside nightstand joints, or along baseboards near sleeping areas. Early clues are subtle, which is why a careful professional inspection matters more than waiting to catch activity in daylight.

pests.name: Common Look-Alikes
pests.blurb: Carpet beetles, spider beetles, booklice, and even young German cockroaches are often mistaken for bed bugs in Florida bedrooms and living rooms. Carpet beetle larvae leave shed skins and damage fabrics but do not feed on blood, while cockroach signs look quite different up close. If you are unsure, save what you found without crushing it and let a trained eye confirm before you treat.

sections.heading: How bed bugs spread in the Orlando tourism corridor
body: The Disney and Orlando tourism corridor brings constant guest turnover, and that movement is ideal for bed bugs. Travelers can unknowingly carry a few bugs home in suitcases, backpacks, jackets, or pillows after a hotel, vacation home, cruise transfer, or timeshare stay. With rentals in Kissimmee, Celebration, Lake Buena Vista, and Orlando turning over week after week, even a well-kept property can pick up an introduction between cleanings.

Local living spreads them further once they arrive. Guests, visiting relatives, college students returning home, and roommates moving between apartments can all move bugs from room to room. Secondhand headboards, mattresses, couches, and bed frames are another common source around Osceola and Orange Counties. That is why we look beyond the main bedroom and trace how people, laundry, and furniture move through your space.

sections.heading: Heat treatment vs. conventional treatment
body: Whole-room heat treatment uses sustained, carefully monitored high heat to warm beds, furniture, walls, and belongings to levels that are lethal for bed bugs in every life stage. Heat reaches into seams, cracks, and clutter where sprays struggle to penetrate, and it addresses eggs along with active bugs in a single service visit. It is often a strong fit for established issues, cluttered rooms, or vacation rentals that need thorough results with minimal residual footprint and faster re-entry for guests.

Conventional treatment uses targeted applications of professional materials, dusts for voids, and growth regulators, paired with detailed preparation and follow-up visits. This approach is often a good fit for early or localized activity, budget-sensitive situations, or spaces with heat-sensitive belongings that need extra care. Many homes do best with a blended plan, and during inspection we will explain the tradeoffs honestly so you can choose with confidence. Either way, success depends on thorough prep, careful coverage, and monitoring afterward.

sections.heading: How to prepare your home (and why DIY fails)
body: Good preparation makes treatment far more effective. We will give you a simple checklist that usually includes laundering bedding and clothing on high heat settings and bagging clean items, reducing clutter around beds, pulling furniture slightly away from walls, and making mattresses and storage areas accessible. For rentals, that also means coordinating with cleaners, handymen, and property managers so every sleeping area can be inspected and serviced at the same time.

Do-it-yourself efforts usually fail because bed bugs sense and avoid many over-the-counter sprays, pushing deeper into walls and neighboring rooms. Foggers scatter them without reaching hidden harborages, and repeated light spraying can encourage resistance while leaving eggs untouched. Home remedies and mattress encasements alone rarely solve the root issue. Professional equipment, product rotation, and patient follow-up are what break the cycle and keep a small introduction from becoming a building-wide concern.

process.detail: We inspect mattresses, box springs, headboards, nightstands, couches, baseboards, and luggage areas with flashlights and careful attention to harborages. We show you what we find and confirm whether activity is bed bugs or a look-alike pest.

We map affected rooms and explain whether heat, conventional service, or a blended approach fits your home and timeline. You receive clear prep guidance and expectations for guest turnover, family life, and pets before we begin.

On service day we treat sleeping areas, furniture joints, cracks, and nearby living spaces with meticulous coverage and care for belongings. For heat projects we monitor temperatures closely, and for conventional work we place materials precisely where bugs travel and hide.

We return to recheck harborages, review interceptor monitors and laundry practices, and address any lingering activity. You leave with simple habits for travel, secondhand furniture, and rental turnovers to lower the risk of reintroduction.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have bed bugs or something else?
faqs.a: Look for clustered bites after sleep, rusty smears on sheets, shed skins, and live bugs tucked along mattress seams or headboard joints. Carpet beetles and German cockroaches cause confusion, so professional identification helps. Call Orlando Pest Pros for a thorough inspection before you buy products or throw out furniture.

faqs.q: Do I have to throw away my mattress and couch?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Modern mattresses and quality furniture usually respond well to treatment when preparation is done carefully. We will tell you honestly if an item is too damaged or heavily harbored to save, but our goal is to protect your belongings whenever possible.

faqs.q: Is heat treatment better than sprays?
faqs.a: Each method has strengths. Heat excels at penetrating clutter and addressing all life stages in hard-to-reach spots during the visit, while conventional service offers targeted residual protection and flexibility for sensitive items. After inspection we recommend the option that fits the extent of activity, your home layout, and your rental schedule.

faqs.q: Can you treat vacation rentals and apartments discreetly?
faqs.a: Yes. We regularly help vacation homes, condos, and multifamily properties across the Orlando tourism corridor and surrounding neighborhoods. We coordinate with hosts, managers, and cleaners, keep vehicles and equipment low-key, and focus on fast communication so you can welcome guests back with confidence.

faqs.q: What should I do after treatment to prevent them from coming back?
faqs.a: Use luggage racks while traveling, dry clothes on high heat after trips, and check secondhand furniture carefully before bringing it inside. Reduce clutter around beds, vacuum seams and baseboards routinely, and let us know quickly if new signs appear. Early follow-up keeps a fresh introduction from spreading through the home.

services.h1: Humane Wildlife Removal in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: Hearing heavy thumps in the attic after dark or finding the lawn rooted up overnight is common in Central Florida, where mild weather keeps wildlife active in every season. Around Kissimmee, Saint Cloud, and Orlando, raccoons, opossums, squirrels, and armadillos live close to homes and use open vents, loose soffits, and easy pet food.

We focus on humane, common-sense wildlife removal that protects your home and treats animals responsibly under Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission guidelines. That means careful identification, live trapping where appropriate, and sealing entry points so the problem does not repeat. If you hear noises, see damage, or notice odor in the attic or under the shed, call Orlando Pest Pros for a calm local assessment.

pests.name: Armadillos
pests.blurb: Armadillos root up lawns and garden beds hunting grubs, leaving pitted turf and scattered mulch across Osceola and Orange County yards. They also burrow under sheds and decks. We combine humane trapping with low barrier fencing to block reentry.

pests.name: Opossums
pests.blurb: Opossums den under sheds, decks, and porches and wander into garages and attics looking for pet food and shelter. They are usually quiet but leave droppings, odor, and overturned trash. We remove them gently and close off den sites.

pests.name: Raccoons
pests.blurb: Raccoons tear at shingles, soffits, and vents to den in attics, especially mothers seeking a safe spot for young. They raid trash, eat citrus and pet food, and leave messy latrines. We use humane trapping and secure exclusion to end the cycle.

pests.name: Gray Squirrels
pests.blurb: Gray squirrels chew through soffits and eaves and nest in warm attics, where they gnaw wiring and insulation and stash food. They travel along oaks, citrus trees, and fences onto roofs. We remove them and seal chewed entries with sturdy materials.

pests.name: Flying Squirrels
pests.blurb: Flying squirrels are small, nocturnal, and social, so a Central Florida attic can hold a colony that scurries most nights. Droppings and a musky odor are common clues. We use humane exclusion doors and careful sealing to move them out without trapping young inside.

pests.name: Bats
pests.blurb: Bats slip into tiny gaps along rooflines and gables and are protected by state rules, so they are never trapped like raccoons. We provide humane bat exclusion with one way exits during the right season, then seal gaps and address guano and odor.

sections.heading: Florida's most common home invaders
body: In Osceola and Orange Counties there is no real off season for wildlife. Neighborhoods near lakes, retention ponds, oak hammocks, citrus trees, and conservation edges offer steady food and shelter, so raccoons, opossums, squirrels, and armadillos stay busy all year. That year round pressure means a loose vent or lifted shingle can turn into a den quickly, often before you notice more than faint scratching.

Each animal leaves its own signature. Armadillos plow lawns and beds and push soil under foundations and sheds. Raccoons and opossums favor attics, crawl spaces, and the dark space under sheds, with nighttime thumps, tipped cans, and strong odor. Squirrels are daytime movers that chew wood and gnaw entry holes, while flying squirrels and bats create soft nighttime rustling and staining near rooflines.

sections.heading: Humane trapping, Florida FWC rules, and relocation
body: Humane removal starts with identification and the least stressful method that works. We favor live cage traps placed safely, exclusion doors that let animals leave but not return, and hands off care for mothers with dependent young whenever possible. We do not use poisons for wildlife, which cause suffering and can harm pets, hawks, and owls, and we handle traps, droppings, and nesting material with protective practices.

Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission rules shape what happens next, and they exist to limit disease spread and protect native species. Rabies vector animals such as raccoons and bats cannot simply be driven to the woods and released, and relocation is generally limited to release on the same property or humane handling by qualified professionals. Bats and other protected species need properly timed exclusion rather than trapping, which is why a local pro who follows FWC guidance matters for both legal compliance and animal welfare.

sections.heading: Exclusion and repair: keeping them out for good
body: Trapping without sealing is only a pause, because Central Florida wildlife will test the same weak spot again. We close gaps along soffits, fascia, roof returns, vents, and plumbing penetrations with chew resistant materials, add chimney caps and vent guards where needed, and screen open areas under sheds and decks with buried hardware cloth. For armadillos we add low trench barriers and tidy harborage, and we recommend keeping tree limbs trimmed well back from the roof and securing trash and pet food.

Attic and den cleanup matters as much as the patch. Raccoon latrines, opossum droppings, and squirrel nesting debris carry odor and bacteria and can attract roof rats and insects if left in insulation. We remove soiled material where accessible, treat and deodorize affected areas, and point out damaged insulation, chewed wiring covers, and stained decking so you can plan repairs that keep the home sealed, dry, and quiet.

process.detail: We walk the roofline, attic, yard, and under structures to find tracks, droppings, rub marks, and entry holes. We identify the species, entry method, and whether young may be present so the plan fits the animal.
We set live traps or exclusion doors in safe, shaded locations and monitor them with care. Mothers and mobile young are handled gently to avoid separating families inside walls or attics.

Once animals are out, we seal entries with sturdy, wildlife resistant materials and reinforce vents, soffits, and shed skirting. Barriers for armadillos and trimming guidance for squirrels help prevent a quick return.

We clear accessible droppings and nesting debris and treat odor sources to make the space less inviting. You get plain advice on trash storage, pet feeding, citrus pickup, and yard upkeep for lasting protection.

faqs.q: Is wildlife removal humane and what happens to the animals?
faqs.a: Yes, our approach favors live trapping, exclusion doors, and careful release practices that reduce stress and avoid poisons. Animals are handled quietly and released on the property where allowed or managed humanely under state guidelines. We also focus on sealing so they do not need to be trapped again.

faqs.q: Why can I not just catch a raccoon and release it in the woods?
faqs.a: Florida FWC rules limit moving raccoons and other rabies vector species because relocation spreads disease and animals often struggle or return. In most cases release must happen on the same property or be handled humanely by qualified professionals. Call Orlando Pest Pros and we will explain lawful options for your situation.

faqs.q: How can I tell what is living in my attic?
faqs.a: Timing and sound help narrow it down, with gray squirrels active by day and raccoons, opossums, flying squirrels, and roof rats more active at night. Look for droppings, odor, chewed soffits, or disturbed insulation, but avoid entering a tight attic alone. A professional inspection confirms the species and finds every entry point.

faqs.q: How do you stop armadillos from tearing up my lawn again?
faqs.a: We remove active armadillos with humane trapping, then add low barriers around sheds, beds, and fence lines and close burrow openings. Reducing dense cover and picking up fallen fruit helps, though grub treatments alone rarely solve digging. Ongoing exclusion is what keeps turf smooth through the seasons.

faqs.q: Do you clean up droppings, odor, and attic mess after removal?
faqs.a: Yes, we remove accessible droppings and nesting material, treat soiled areas, and help reduce lingering odor that draws new pests. We will point out stained or compressed insulation and chewed materials so you can plan repairs. Sealing entries at the same time keeps raccoons, squirrels, and roof rats from reusing the space.
